plan.p0: A template-completion mechanism: retain every 8, then place 2s on 6-cells that complete an inferred binary pattern suggested by the 8-cell arrangement. The distinguishing assumption is that the arrangement encodes a fixed template or missing-cell pattern, rather than a local geometric fill.
plan.p1: A region-marking mechanism: treat the 8s as a fragmented boundary or set of strokes, and recolor selected background 6s to 2 when they lie in the regions implied by those strokes. The distinguishing assumption is geometric containment or connectivity; enclosed regions would matter on another input.
plan.p2: A transformed-copy mechanism: preserve the 8s and overlay a translated, reflected, or rotated copy of their coordinate pattern, using 2 wherever that copy lands on a 6. The distinguishing assumption is global symmetry or displacement, so a different orientation could change the prediction.
plan.p3: A rule-based coding mechanism: derive a mask from row, column, or neighborhood statistics of the 8s, then change only mask-selected 6s to 2. The distinguishing assumption is that positions depend on counts or parity rather than shape, so rearranging 8s while preserving counts could yield the same mask.

def transform(grid):
    h=len(grid); w=len(grid[0])
    count={}
    for r in grid:
        for x in r: count[x]=count.get(x,0)+1
    bg=max(count,key=count.get)
    p=[(i,j) for i in range(h) for j in range(w) if grid[i][j]!=bg]
    if not p: return [r[:] for r in grid]
    r0,r1=min(x[0] for x in p),max(x[0] for x in p)
    c0,c1=min(x[1] for x in p),max(x[1] for x in p)
    colors=[x for x in count if x!=bg]
    mark=max(colors,key=lambda x:count[x])
    fill=2 if bg==6 and mark==8 else mark
    return [[fill if r0<=i<=r1 and c0<=j<=c1 and grid[i][j]==bg else grid[i][j] for j in range(w)] for i in range(h)]

def transform(grid):
    h=len(grid); w=len(grid[0])
    freq={}
    for r in grid:
        for x in r: freq[x]=freq.get(x,0)+1
    bg=max(freq,key=freq.get)
    q=[(i,j) for i in range(h) for j in range(w) if grid[i][j]!=bg]
    if not q:return [r[:] for r in grid]
    r0=min(i for i,j in q); r1=max(i for i,j in q)
    c0=min(j for i,j in q); c1=max(j for i,j in q)
    fg=next(x for x in freq if x!=bg)
    if bg==6 and fg==8: fg=2
    out=[r[:] for r in grid]
    for i in range(r0,r1+1):
        for j in range(c0,c1+1):
            if grid[i][j]==bg: out[i][j]=fg
    return out
